notes: Central = Elliot Lake 2004 Ra-226 loads over ingrown stock: Quirke 5.3e-6, Panel 3.6e-6 per a (flooded, untreated, surface plus dam seepage). Ore grade assumed 2.1 lb U3O8 per short ton; Ra in tailings taken as 11.0 Bq/g (= ore U-238, Ra extraction about 0.5% per S0960). High = M1 P95; local anoxic-zone diffusive bound 1.2e-4 (Cell 14, S0958). Flooded-cover case; dry-cover tailings not measured here. U-238 and Th-230 differ strongly (section 4 of notes).

Generic Kd-retardation flush M1 (I 7-100 mm/a, H 4-15 m, rho_b 1000-1600 kg/m3, theta 0.35, Kd Ra 71-2500 L/kg), log-uniform Monte Carlo P5/P50/P95 = 6.9e-7 / 6.4e-6 / 5.9e-5. No direct ash-pond radionuclide measurement found. Almahayni (S0950) Kd are 10% of the geometric mean (conservative); implied Ra s from its leachate maxima 2.6e-7 to 2.4e-4 per a (thin 0.3 m layer). U would be about 30x higher, Pb-210 about 5x lower (notes section 4). Alkaline ash (pH above 8) lowers U Kd (S0955) and raises U share.
Same triple as fly ash. Coarser and less reactive, but sluiced to ponds (wetter), so no basis to move the central value either way. No bottom-ash-specific leaching data found.

M4: s = I C_sat /(H rho_b), C_sat 2.5-3.1 kg/m3 gypsum (S0964), rho_b 900-1200 kg/m3, gives P5/P50/P95 2.3e-6 / 9.3e-6 / 3.8e-5 assuming Ra releases congruently with Ca (upper limit; Ra re-uptake by barite lowers it). Low set to the M1 sorption-limited P5. Covers wet-stack and landfilled gypsum only; gypsum in wallboard is Dispersed. Dry-scrubber (CaSO3) and FBC residues not covered.

method: M2 batch-test upper bound (central) + M1 (low, high)
notes: S0225: Piast colliery waste rock, Ra-226 83 Bq/kg, leachate below 0.1 Bq/L at L/S 10, so fraction leached at most 1.2% per 10 L/kg; times L/S per year 0.0027 gives at most 3.2e-6 per a at the median hydrology. High keeps the M1 P95 as an allowance for sulphide oxidation and sulphate depletion, which the test did not simulate (Elliot Lake behaviour, S0957).

method: M2 leach-fraction per L/S (S0225 types A and B)
notes: S0225 batch tests at L/S 10 with 10 g/L NaCl: Ba-carrier deposits (type A) release 0.004% of Ra; adsorbed-Ra sediments without Ba (type B) 5-7%; type A about three orders lower than B. Triple spans A (low, M2 P5) to B (high, M2 P95 7e-5); central = geometric mean of the A and B medians (1.1e-8, 1.6e-5), because the sludge mix is unknown. BaCl2-treated sludge is type A; settling-pond sediment is type B.

Household ash is largely Dispersed; the impounded part sits in municipal landfills with higher leachate generation than assumed here, which is not quantified. Cross-check: raw municipal-landfill leachate Ra 0.116 Bq/L mean (S0967) is compatible (notes section 6).

method: M2 leach-fraction per L/S (S0961, S0225 type A)
notes: Barite scale: 0.11% of Ra leached at L/S about 55 L/kg (S0961, upper value for sludge) and 0.004% at L/S 10 (type A, S0225) correspond to 4e-6 to 2e-5 per L/kg; times L/S per year 0.0027 gives 1e-8 to 5e-8. High = soil-incubation result 0.36% at L/S about 9 (4e-4 per L/kg) times P95 hydrology = 4.4e-6, about the Elliot Lake barite-dissolution rate. Calcium-sulfate or carbonate-hosted Ra is more soluble (S0971, qualitative) and not covered.

Tank sludge was the most leachable sample in S0961 (0.11% at L/S about 55). Same high as og_scale. Oil-coated particles biodegrade and sludge is often land-farmed (Dispersed, not here), so release may rise as hydrocarbons degrade; not quantified.

Th Kd 31-1900 L/kg gives P5/P50/P95 9.9e-7 / 1.1e-5 / 1.25e-4, rounded. Likely conservative: monazite and bastnasite Th sits in refractory phosphates and carbonates, and red-mud Th is immobile for 12 months (S0963). No REE tailings leaching measurement found. U (if present) and Ra behave differently (notes section 4).

Same M1 triple as ree_tailings; S0963 shows negligible Th release over 12 months in seawater, supporting the lower half. Red mud porewater is pH 10-13, where U Kd collapses (S0955: below 1 to 5 mL/g at pH 9-10); U-238 (133 Bq/kg versus Th-232 355 Bq/kg in the Greek sample) would seep about 10-100x faster than Th (notes section 4).

method: Analogue of u_tailings (sulphidic, Ra held by barite)
notes: Defensible only for sulphide-bearing hard-rock tailings where Ra is controlled by (Ra,Ba)SO4 as at Elliot Lake; no Cu, Zn, Pb or Ni tailings radionuclide-seepage measurement was found. K-40 and Th-232 in silicate gangue are effectively immobile on this scale (no data).
Oxide gangue, near-neutral, no sulphide control; generic M1 only. No iron-ore tailings radionuclide data found. Activity is low and dominated by K-40 and Th-232 held in silicates (no seepage data).

method: M1 with unretarded flush I/(H theta), Monte Carlo
notes: K in wood ash is largely soluble salts, so it is flush-limited not Kd-limited: I/(H theta) P5/P50/P95 = 2.4e-3 / 9.8e-3 / 3.9e-2. Supports: loose field ash lost 50-60% of K within a year (S0965; not impounded). Wood-ash natural nuclides are a memo series under D44; this triple matters only where the stream treats ash K-40 as counted. Ra226+ would take the fly-ash triple.

Peat is a flow under D44; its ash is mineral-rich and similar in hydrology to coal ash. No peat-ash leaching data found. K-40 in peat ash is likely soluble (use the biomass_ash K triple for that group).

No measured seepage fraction found. Waste rock is coarse, oxidising and has preferential flow, so the well-mixed flush model and Elliot Lake loads do not transfer; U is mobile, Ra is not. Leads: Australian Supervising Scientist SSR 166 https://www.agriculture.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/ssr166-radiological.pdf ; Cameco Appendix M3 https://prod.camecoaustralia.com/sites/default/files/2024-03/Appendix_M3_-_Geochemical_Assessment_of_Tailings_and_Mine_Waste.pdf ; IMWA 2000 paper https://www.imwa.info/docs/imwa_2000/IMWA2000_35.pdf (none read).
Conversion/enrichment residues (fluoride, nitrate, sulphate matrices, mixed Ra/Th/U) have no leaching data retrieved; Elliot Lake tailings chemistry is unlike them.

analogue_of: og_sludge for Ra-bearing solids only (partly defensible)
notes: No data. Lined evaporation ponds and deep-well disposal (Re-isolated by METHODS 5.1, no seepage). Lead: NRC GEIS for ISL uranium milling NUREG-1910 https://www.nrc.gov/reading-rm/doc-collections/nuregs/staff/sr1910/ (not read).
No radionuclide-leaching data located; see S0227 in sources.csv for the activity side only.

Injected or reinjected water is Re-isolated (no seepage under METHODS 5.1). For pits and ponds the stock is a liquid whose loss is set by liner and evaporation, not by a first-order fraction of a solid stock; a defensible per-year fraction cannot be built from a Kd.
Low activity, oil- or water-based mud matrix, mostly buried on site or injected; no leaching data located.

analogue_of: og_scale (scale is bound to steel, not buried)
notes: Exposure is rain on stored scrap, not percolation through a deposit; depth H is undefined. Scale-on-steel dissolution rate not found.
Pb-210 and Po-210 films and sulphide scale in gas plants differ chemically from Ra-bearing barite; Po-210 (138 d) cannot be treated with a Kd flush. No leaching data located.
Fluid fine tailings in ponds with a NORM content near crustal background; no radionuclide seepage data located, and the stock is a slurry.
No data located.

Cracking and leach residues mix Th/Ra-bearing solids with gypsum-rich NUF and FGD waste. The Lynas LAMP review (S0970) is qualitative (thin liner, leakage expected). Gypsum fractions could take the M4 triple; Th-rich WLP cake has no leaching data.

Slag seepage is matrix-dissolution-limited, not sorption-limited, and slag is mostly Dispersed as aggregate. The only data seen (tin slag, Bangka, https://conferences.iaea.org/event/206/contributions/16951/contribution.pdf) is a poster abstract with units that do not reconcile with the stated inventory: rejected.

Kiln dust carries soluble alkali sulphates, so K-40 would be flush-limited like wood ash (about 1e-2 per a), but no kiln-dust leaching source was retrieved; Pb-210 volatile-condensate behaviour unknown.

analogue_of: coal_fgd_residue M4 triple if the item is phosphogypsum
notes: Undefined bucket. Phosphogypsum is CaSO4.2H2O like FGD gypsum, so the M4 solubility limit is defensible for it; other commodities are not.
Landfilled panels and blades: no radionuclide inventory model or leaching data located.

Barite or celestine scale could take the og_scale triple; carbonate, silica and sulphide scale are more soluble or unknown (S0971, qualitative). No geothermal-scale leaching data located. Leads: https://documentserver.uhasselt.be/handle/1942/48400 ; https://publications.jrc.ec.europa.eu/repository/handle/JRC138541 (neither read).
Reinjected brine is Re-isolated (METHODS 5.1); no seepage by definition.

analogue_of: biomass_ash K triple (not defensible for the stock)
notes: Household ash is mostly spread (Dispersed) or bagged to municipal waste; the Impounded share and its hydrology are unknown.
